L188: # FRET: Formal Requirements Elicitation Tool
L189: ## Introduction
L190: FRET is a framework for the elicitation, specification, formalization, and analysis of system requirements. It enables users to specify unambiguous requirements using restricted English sentences while providing multiple representations to enhance clarity and validation of semantics. These representations include natural language descriptions, formal mathematical logics, and visual diagrams, allowing users with different expertise to review and understand the precise meaning of each requirement.
L191: FRET supports hierarchical requirement definition, enabling users to organize requirements based on different levels. It also offers export capabilities in various formats, facilitating integration with external formal analysis tools. FRET provides automated, requirement-based test case generation, incorporating a coverage metric to assess the adequacy of generated tests.
L192: Furthermore, FRET includes built-in consistency checking mechanisms to detect conflicts between requirements and thus, it helps to ensure that requirements are complete and correct.
L193: For more details, refer to the 【86†FRET manual】.

L237: # 🌱 Spec Kit
L238: 
L239: ### Build with a spec, fix a bug, or assess an idea — with your coding agent.
L240: 
L241: English · 【109†简体中文】 · 【106†日本語】 · 【107†한국어】
L242: 
L243: Spec Kit is an open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes. Start with a ready-made process, customize it, or bring your own.
L244: ## Choose your process
L245: What you need  | Process  | Outcome
L246: --- | --- | ---
L247: Build a feature or application  | 【116†Spec-Driven Development】  | A specification carried through planning, implementation, and convergence
L248: Diagnose and repair broken behavior  | 【117†Bug fixing】  | An assessed cause, scoped fix, and recorded verification
L249: Decide whether an idea deserves investment  | 【118†Idea assessment】  | An evidence-backed go, clarify, or stop decision
L250: Adopt or create a different process  | 【119†Your own process】  | A process adapted or assembled from reusable primitives
L251: These are independent entry points, not mandatory phases. SDD ships in core; bug fixing and assessment are bundled extensions you install when needed, and the primitives below let you adopt or create other processes.
L252: ## Capabilities
L253: 
L254: Spec Kit combines ready-to-use processes with composable mechanisms:
L255: Capability  | Spec Kit mechanism
L256: --- | ---
L257: Connect to or switch between coding agents  | 【120†Integration†github.github.io】
L258: Add a command, quality gate, or complete process  | 【121†Extension†github.github.io】
L259: Connect a process to an external tool or service  | 【121†Extension†github.github.io】
L260: React to coding-agent lifecycle events  | 【122†Extension runtime event†github.github.io】
L261: Run extension commands before or after Spec Kit commands  | 【123†Extension hook†github.github.io】
L262: Adapt templates, commands, terminology, or methodology  | 【124†Preset†github.github.io】
L263: Enforce organizational or regulatory standards  | 【124†Preset†github.github.io】
L264: Override a template for one project  | 【125†Project-local override†github.github.io】
L265: Automate prompts, commands, gates, and shell tasks  | 【126†Workflow†github.github.io】
L266: Modify an installed workflow without forking it  | 【127†Workflow overlay†github.github.io】
L267: Add reusable executable behavior to workflows  | 【128†Workflow step†github.github.io】
L268: Install a curated setup for a role or team  | 【129†Bundle†github.github.io】
L269: Discover community components  | 【130†Catalog†github.github.io】
L270: Host a private catalog of approved components  | 【130†Catalog†github.github.io】
L271: Access private catalogs and component downloads  | 【131†Authentication†github.github.io】
L272: Work offline or behind a firewall  | 【132†Local sources and self-hosted catalogs†github.github.io】
L273: Inspect which layer supplies a command, template, or script  | 【133†Artifact inventory†github.github.io】
L274: Search the active catalogs with commands such as `specify extension search`, `specify preset search`, `specify workflow search`, and `specify bundle search`. Spec Kit includes community catalogs, and organizations can add their own curated sources. Catalog listings are not audits or endorsements, so review community source code before installing or running it.
L275: ## Get started
L276: 
L277: You need Python 3.11+, 【134†uv†github.github.io】, and a supported AI coding agent on Linux, macOS, or Windows.
L278: 
L279: Run these commands in your terminal to install Spec Kit and create a project. This example uses GitHub Copilot.
L280: 
L281:     uv tool install specify-cli
L282:     specify init my-project --integration copilot
L283:     cd my-project
L284: 
L285: After installing the Specify CLI and creating your project, launch your coding agent in the project directory, then choose a process below.
L286: 
L287: For other setups:
L288:   * 【135†Installation†github.github.io】 for pinned releases, other installers, CI, and troubleshooting.
L289:   * 【136†Existing projects†github.github.io】 to start with code you already have.
L290:   * 【120†Other agents†github.github.io】 for integration keys and 【137†invocation syntax†github.github.io】.
L291:   * 【138†Upgrade†github.github.io】 to update an existing installation.
L292: ## Spec-Driven Development
L293: 
L294: Define what to build and why, then turn the specification into a plan, tasks, and working code.
L295: 
L296: The minimal flow is shown below. Create a constitution once per project and repeat the remaining steps for each feature. Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing.
L297: This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its 【137†equivalent invocation syntax†github.github.io】.
L298: 
L299:     `/speckit-constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing, and maintainability.
L300:     /speckit-specify Build a photo organizer with albums grouped by date and a tile preview of each album.
L301:     /speckit-plan Use Vite with vanilla JavaScript. Keep images local and store metadata in SQLite.
L302:     /speckit-tasks
L303:     /speckit-implement
L304:     /speckit-converge
L305:     `
L306: Repeat implement and converge until convergence reports `Converged`. For clarification, checklists, and consistency analysis, see the SDD walkthrough.
L307: 
L308: 【139†SDD walkthrough†github.github.io】 · 【140†Command reference†github.github.io】
L309: ## Bug fixing
L310: 
L311: Assess the cause, fix the bug, and verify the original symptom is resolved. No SDD feature workflow is required first.
L312: 
L313: Install the bug-fixing extension in your terminal, from the project directory:
L314: 
L315:     specify extension add bug
L316: 
L317: Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing.
L318: This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its 【137†equivalent invocation syntax†github.github.io】.
L319: 
L320:     `/speckit-bug-assess "Submitting an empty password crashes the login form." slug=login-crash
L321:     /speckit-bug-fix slug=login-crash
L322:     /speckit-bug-test slug=login-crash
L323:     `
L324: 
L325: Review the reports in `.specify/bugs/login-crash/`. The final verdict is `verified`, `partial`, or `failed`; only `verified` confirms a successful fix.
L326: 【141†Bug-fixing walkthrough†github.github.io】 · 【142†Command reference†github.github.io】
L327: ## Idea assessment
L328: 
L329: Gather evidence to decide whether an idea is worth pursuing. No source code or SDD feature workflow is required.
L330: 
L331: Install the assessment extension in your terminal, from the project directory:
L332: 
L333:     specify extension add assess
L334: 
L335: Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing.
